topicTitle: 9.1 Maximum and Minimum Values of Trigonometric Functions
stem:
Find the maximum and minimum values of the following trigonometric functions.
(i) $\mathrm{y}=2-2 \operatorname{Cos} \theta$
(ii) $\mathrm{y}=\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{2} \operatorname{Sin} \theta$
(iii) $\mathrm{y}=\frac{1}{5}-2 \operatorname{Sin}(3 \theta-7)$
(iv) $\mathrm{y}=7+\frac{3}{5} \operatorname{Cos}(2 \theta-1)$

topicTitle: 9.1 Maximum and Minimum Values of Trigonometric Functions
stem:
Find the maximum and minimum values of the following reciprocal trigonometric functions.
(i) $\mathrm{y}=\frac{1}{4+3 \operatorname{Sin} \theta}$
(ii) $\mathrm{y}=\frac{1}{\frac{1}{2}-5 \operatorname{Cos} \theta}$
(iii) $\mathrm{y}=\frac{1}{\frac{1}{3}-4 \operatorname{Sin}(2 \theta-5)}$
(iv) $\mathrm{y}=\frac{1}{3+\frac{2}{5} \sin (5 \theta-7)}$

topicTitle: 9.1 Maximum and Minimum Values of Trigonometric Functions
stem:
Find domain and range of the following:
(i) $y=7 \operatorname{Cos} 4 x$
(ii) $\mathrm{y}=\operatorname{Cos} \frac{x}{3}$
(iii) $\mathrm{y}=\operatorname{Sin} \frac{2 x}{3}$
(iv) $y=7 \operatorname{Cot} \frac{\pi}{2} x$
(v) $y=4 \operatorname{Tan} \pi x$
(vi) $\mathrm{y}=\operatorname{Cosec} 4 x$

topicTitle: 9.1 Maximum and Minimum Values of Trigonometric Functions
stem:
Find the periods of the following:
(i) $y=6 \operatorname{Sec}(2 x-3)$
(ii) $y=\operatorname{Cos}(5 x+4)$
(iii) $y=\operatorname{Cot} 4 x+\operatorname{Sin} \frac{5 x}{2}$
(iv) $y=7 \operatorname{Sin}(3 x+3)$
(v) $y=5 \operatorname{Sin}(2 x+3)$
(vi) $y=2 \operatorname{Tan} 3 x+7 \operatorname{Cos} 5 x$

Check whether the following functions are odd or even?
(i) $y=\operatorname{Sin} x+x \operatorname{Cos} x$
(ii) $y=x^{3} \operatorname{Sin} x \operatorname{Cos} x$
(iii) $y=\frac{x^{2} \operatorname{Tan} x}{x+\operatorname{Sin} x}$
(iv) $y=x^{3} \operatorname{Sin} x \operatorname{Cos}^{2} x$
(v) $y=\frac{\operatorname{Sin}^{2} x}{x+\operatorname{Tan} x}$
(vi) $y=\frac{\operatorname{Tan} x-\operatorname{Sin} x}{\operatorname{Sin}^{3} x}$
(vii) $y=\frac{\operatorname{Sec} x}{x+\operatorname{Tan} x}$
(viii) $y=x^{2} \operatorname{Sin} x-\operatorname{Cot} x$

Draw the graph of each of the following functions:
(i) $y=2 \operatorname{Sin} x$
(ii) $y=2 \operatorname{Cos} 3 x$
(iii) $y=2 \operatorname{Tan} 2 x$
(iv) $\mathrm{y}=\operatorname{Cos} \frac{x}{2}$
(v) $y=2 \operatorname{Sin} 3 x$
(vi) $y=3 \operatorname{Cos} x$
(vii) $y=\operatorname{Cos}^{2} x$
(viii) $y=\operatorname{Sin}^{2} x$
(ix) $y=\operatorname{Tan}^{2} x$
(x) $y=\operatorname{Sin} \frac{x}{2}$
Draw the graphs of $y=\operatorname{Sin} x$ and $y=\operatorname{Sin} 2 x$ in $[0,2 \pi]$ on the same scale.
Draw the graphs of $y=\operatorname{Cos} x$ and $y=\operatorname{Cos} 2 x$ in $[0,2 \pi]$ on the same scale.

Solve graphically:
(i) $\operatorname{Sin} x=\operatorname{Cos} x$
(ii) $\operatorname{Cos} x=x$
(iii) $\operatorname{Sin} x=x$
(iv) $\operatorname{Tan} x=x$

Alternating current cyclically reverses direction. The maximum voltage is about 180 volts when the standard frequency is 56 Hz (56 cycles per second). The voltage can be modeled by
$$
V(t)=a \operatorname{Sin}(k(t-d))+c
$$
Determine each of the following:
    a. Period of 56 Hz AC,
    b. The value of k,
    c. The amplitude of the voltage function,
    d. Model the voltage with an appropriate transformed Sine function.

A Ferris Wheel has a diameter of 17 m. You board at the bottom of the Ferris Wheel from a platform 2 m off the ground. If it takes 25 seconds to reach the top, determine an equation for the height of a rider with respect to time.

The pendulum of a clock swings with a periodic motion that can be represented by a trigonometric function. At rest, the pendulum is 16 cm above the base. The highest point of the swing is 20 cm above the base, and it take 2 seconds for the pendulum to swing back and forth to its starting point once. Assume the pendulum is released from its highest point. Write a cosine equation that models the height of the pendulum as a function of time.
